summary: Verified Statement Decoder visual edit: screenshot-tour replaced with how-to walkthrough video on web (logged-out AND logged-in) and mobile (public tool). Web passes all checks. Mobile card + heading + video element all render with correct .mp4 source and HTML5 controls; the only caveat is that expo-video VideoView does not propagate testID='sd-how-to-video-player' to the underlying <video> DOM node on web preview (works on native builds).

ui_bugs.issue: testID='sd-how-to-video-player' is not forwarded to the underlying <video> element in the Expo web preview DOM, so automated selectors can't target the player directly. The video itself renders correctly inside the card [data-testid='sd-how-to-video'] with .mp4 src + controls. On native iOS/Android this testID still maps to accessibility identifier; the issue is web-preview-only.

parity_issues.issue: Web exposes testID on the <video> element (data-testid='sd-how-to-video-player'); mobile Expo web preview does not (expo-video VideoView swallows testID). Visual + functional parity is intact; only automated-selector parity differs.
parity_issues.expected: Both surfaces expose a selectable player element at [data-testid=sd-how-to-video-player]
parity_issues.actual: Web exposes it; mobile exposes only the card [data-testid=sd-how-to-video] in the web-preview DOM

action_items: (Optional, low priority) On mobile, wrap the <VideoView ... testID='sd-how-to-video-player' /> in a <View testID='sd-how-to-video-player'> (or add an outer host View with the testID) so automated web-preview tests can target the player element directly. No functional change required — the video already plays and renders correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: Web <video> currently has no poster image; on first paint the frame area is black until metadata loads. Adding a lightweight poster would improve perceived performance (not required by request).

Both surfaces hardcode the same HOW_TO_VIDEO_URL constant in two files. If the asset ever moves, both files must be edited. Consider centralising via a shared constants module or asset manifest (minor, not in scope).
test_credentials: cathy@example.com / testpass123 (used for logged-in web check)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Statement Decoder /ai-tools/statement-decoder (web) and /tool/statement-decoder (mobile) now show a 'How to use the Statement Decoder' walkthrough video instead of the old screenshot tour. Web section data-testid='sd-how-to-video', video player data-testid='sd-how-to-video-player' (HTML5 <video>, mp4, controls). Mobile card testID='sd-how-to-video' contains an expo-video VideoView; the <video> inside the card loads the same mp4 but the inner testID is not reflected in the web-preview DOM, so target the outer card data-testid or query 'video' inside the card. Both logged-out and logged-in users see the section on web; mobile tool screen is public.
rca of the issue: expo-video's <VideoView> on react-native-web does not spread the testID prop to the underlying <video> element; it only applies accessibilityLabel-related attributes. Confirmed by DOM probe: card has data-testid='sd-how-to-video' but only one <video> inside with no data-testid. Mitigation: wrap VideoView in a host <View testID='sd-how-to-video-player'> on the mobile side.
